# PR #4869: Patch: `play_ai_turn` called twice on one game gives every action a nonce the game has not seen

Closes #4786

## What changed and why

`play_ai_turn` (`crates/ai/src/match_.rs`) minted nonces `t0, t1, …` from zero on every call. A second call on the same game replayed the first turn's nonces, which the engine answers unchanged with `error: None` (§9.3 dedupe) — so the swallowed decisions were still recorded as played. The fix, exactly per plan:

- Before minting, skip any `t{n}` already in `current.applied` (probing `current`, so nonces minted earlier in the same turn are covered too; same probe pattern as `nonce_for` in `crates/engine/src/subsystems/ai_policy.rs`).
- The loop bound changed from `n < AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS` to `actions.len() < AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS`, so skips never eat the turn's action ceiling. On a fresh game the skip is a no-op and `n == actions.len()` holds, so single-call behavior is bit-identical.
- Doc comment updated. No new constants (rule 9), no ruling (bug against the existing README Matches contract plus §9.3, not an open rules decision).
- New regression test `a_second_play_ai_turn_on_the_same_game_applies_every_action_it_returns` in `mod surface_play_ai_turn` (`crates/ai/tests/ai/surface.rs`), verbatim from the issue; the existing `t0…` pin is untouched.

- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai surface_play_ai_turn` — 2 passed (new test plus existing pin).
- Fix temporarily reverted to prove the new test fails: it fails with the issue's exact message, ``p2's action t0 (Play { instance_id: "c6", … }) changed nothing: its nonce was p1's``.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean. `cargo fmt --check` — clean.

````text
# #4786: Patch: `play_ai_turn` called twice on one game gives every action a nonce the game has not seen
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

`play_ai_turn` (`crates/ai/src/match_.rs:488`) numbers its actions `t0, t1, …` from 0 on every call. The engine answers an action whose nonce is already in `state.applied` (the last `NONCE_HISTORY`, 64) as a replay: the state comes back unchanged with `error: None` (`crates/engine/src/reduce.rs`, the nonce check). So a second `play_ai_turn` on the state a first one left has its first decisions swallowed: each costs a full `decide`, changes nothing, and is still pushed onto `actions` and `decisions` as if it had been played, because the loop stops only on an error.

Example: p1's turn through `play_ai_turn` applies `t0` (a play) and `t1` (End turn). `play_ai_turn(&first.state, P2, …)` then returns four actions: `t0` and `t1` are the same play of `c6`, answered as replays of p1's nonces, then `t2` (the play, now applied) and `t3` (End turn). A turn that follows a k-action turn loses its first k decisions and that much of its `AI_TURN_MAX_ACTIONS` ceiling.

Only tests and puzzles call the function today, each once per game, so no shipped game is affected. It is a trap for the next test that plays two turns with it: its `actions` would not be what was played.

### What should happen

Every action `play_ai_turn` returns is one the engine applied (`crates/ai/README.md`, Matches: "`play_ai_turn` plays one AI turn out"). `play_match` already avoids the clash with `m{log.len()}`.

### How to reproduce

Fails on `main` (3a83bd7). Also on branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`, `crates/ai/tests/audit_decks.rs`.

```rust
use jackioh_ai::{AI_GATE_BUDGET, AiOptions, play_ai_turn};
use jackioh_engine::testkit::{Action, PlayerId, create_rng, hash_state, json, reduce, scenario};
const P1: PlayerId = PlayerId::P1;
const P2: PlayerId = PlayerId::P2;

#[test]
fn a_second_play_ai_turn_on_the_same_game_applies_every_action_it_returns() {
    jackioh_cards::register_all();
    let start = scenario(json!({
        "seed": "audit-turns", "active": "p1", "turn": 9,
        "p1": { "hand": ["core-025", "core-011"], "mana": 4, "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-019"] },
        "p2": { "hand": ["core-025", "core-011"], "mana": 4, "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-019"] },
    })).state().clone();
    let mut ai = AiOptions::with_budget(create_rng("audit-turns", 0), AI_GATE_BUDGET);
    let first = play_ai_turn(&start, P1, &mut ai);
    assert!(first.actions.len() >= 2, "p1 plays and ends its turn");
    let second = play_ai_turn(&first.state, P2, &mut ai);

    let mut current = first.state.clone();
    for action in &second.actions {
        let next = reduce(&current, &Action::new(action.body.clone(), P2, action.nonce.clone()));
        assert!(next.error.is_none());
        assert_ne!(hash_state(&next.state), hash_state(&current),
            "p2's action {} ({:?}) changed nothing: its nonce was p1's", action.nonce, action.body);
        current = next.state;
    }
}
```

Output today: ``assertion `left != right` failed: p2's action t0 (Play { instance_id: "c6", … }) changed nothing: its nonce was p1's``.

### Where

The AI: `crates/ai/src/match_.rs`, `play_ai_turn`.

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Make the nonce unique within a game: skip any `t{n}` already in `state.applied`, or number from the game's own count. Skipping keeps `t0, t1, …` for a first call, which a test pins.
- The format is a pinned surface: `docs/polish/3-ai.md` says "nonces `t${n}`", and `crates/ai/tests/ai/surface.rs` has `plays_decides_actions_with_nonces_t0_t1_until_the_ai_owes_nothing`. Keep both true for a first call, or change both in the same pull request.
- No existing test chains two calls on one game (checked: every caller in `crates/ai/tests` makes one call per state), so nothing else should move.

Found by an audit of the AI crate; the reproduction was run and the code path read before filing.
